newsitem.title: UK: Blair pledges tough spending controls indefinitely.
newsitem.headline: Blair pledges tough spending controls indefinitely.

text.p: Tony Blair, leader of Britain's opposition Labour party, saidon Monday that his party would keep tough public spending limits indefinitely if it won the election on May 1.
"The era of tax and spend is dead and buried," he said in a keynote speech to financiers in the City of London.
"I accept the need for economic discipline and embrace the role of free enterprise in the economy. There will be no retreat from any of that."
Blair reaffirmed Labour's determination to match the Conservative government's inflation target of 2.5 percent or less.

Labour would achieve the "golden rule" of public finance, which means the government borrows only to invest, and ensure that the ratio of public debt to gross domestic product (GDP) was stabilised over the economic cycle at a low and prudent level.
Blair said the Conservatives had doubled Britain's national debt since 1989 and repeatedly postponed the date by which the budget deficit would be brought under control.
"We must hit and maintain tough limits into the indefinite future," he said.

Aides described the speech as possibly the most important of the election campaign. It was intended to complete the process of change Blair began when he persuaded his party to ditch its commitment to nationalisation of key industries.
